title: AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch (text based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026). Providers must design systems that interact directly with people so they are informed it is AI unless obvious; information clear, distinguishable, accessible and at the latest at first interaction; paragraph 7 marked amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI.

title: Transparency obligations under Article 50 of the AI Act (questions and answers, updated 24 July 2026)
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Chatbots, AI agents and avatars as examples; four cumulative criteria; obvious exception read restrictively; notice from the first interaction; deployer duties are for emotion recognition, deepfakes and published text; fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide turnover; national market surveillance authorities enforce; no grace period stated for Article 50(1).

title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 20 July 2026, last updated 5 November 2026; the Commission adopted the guidelines; Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026.

title: AI Act, Article 111: AI systems already placed on the market or put into service
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. New paragraph 4 (Digital Omnibus on AI): providers of systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.

title: AI Act, Article 113: Entry into force and application
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. General application date 2 August 2026 (covers Article 50); high-risk duties moved to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I); amendments marked as from the Digital Omnibus on AI.

title: AI Act, Article 4: AI literacy
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Providers and deployers must take measures to build AI literacy of staff and others operating AI on their behalf; Commission and Member States support SMEs; paragraphs marked amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI.

title: AI Privacy Risks & Mitigations: Large Language Models (LLMs) (Support Pool of Experts report, April 2025)
publisher: European Data Protection Board (report by an external expert, Isabel Barberá)
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with a text extractor. Views are the author's, not the EDPB's. First use case is a customer-query chatbot: not high-risk under the AI Act but GDPR risk factors justify starting a DPIA; mitigations include informing users, minimising or anonymising logs, retrieval filters, output redaction, retention policies and rights requests reaching logs.

title: Complying with consumer law when using AI agents (published 9 March 2026, updated 30 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Businesses are responsible for AI agents as for employees, even if a third party supplies them; consider labelling so customers do not think a person is serving them; do not overstate AI; accurate answers on prices, products and rights; human in the loop; test and monitor; fines up to 10% of worldwide turnover.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: plans for commencement (updated 12 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Main Part 5 data protection changes in force 5 February 2026; the Information Commissioner's Office replaced by the Information Commission on 30 September 2026.

title: California Business and Professions Code, Division 7, Part 3, Chapter 6: Bots (sections 17940 to 17943)
supports: Search-confirmed (fetch blocked with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact page. Unlawful to use a bot to communicate with a person in California online with intent to mislead about its artificial identity to incentivise a sale or influence a vote; clear and conspicuous disclosure avoids liability; added by SB 1001 (2018).

title: AB-410 Bots: disclosure (bill status)
supports: Search-confirmed (the leginfo site blocks automated fetches): a search result showed this exact page. AB 410 would require bots to disclose at first contact and answer truthfully when asked; last recorded action 29 August 2025, held under submission in committee.

title: S.B. 226 Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Amendments (2025, enrolled)
supports: Search-confirmed (the site refused connections at fetch time): a search result showed this exact document. Disclosure of generative AI when a consumer clearly and unambiguously asks; prominent disclosure at the outset for high-risk interactions in regulated occupations; safe harbour for clear and conspicuous disclosure.

title: FTC announces crackdown on deceptive AI claims and schemes (25 September 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Operation AI Comply; using AI to deceive is illegal under existing law; DoNotPay marketed a robot lawyer without testing it against human lawyers and agreed to pay $193,000.

title: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149 (decision of 14 February 2024)
supports: Search-confirmed (fetch blocked with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact decision page. The chatbot said a bereavement fare could be claimed after travel; Air Canada argued it was not liable for information from its agents including the chatbot; the tribunal found negligent misrepresentation and awarded the fare difference with interest and fees (about C$812 in total per published reports).

title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month (27 February 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 2.3 million conversations, two-thirds of chats, work of 700 full-time agents, satisfaction on par with humans, 25% fewer repeat inquiries, under 2 minutes vs 11, 23 markets and 35+ languages; customers can still choose live agents. Company claims.

title: Fin AI Agent resolutions (updated 23 September 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Confirmed vs assumed resolutions; explicit requests for a human are not billed; Fin is priced per outcome, at most one per conversation.

title: Hand off to a live agent (Microsoft Copilot Studio)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page dated 30 Apr 2026, updated 19 Aug 2026). Escalate system topic and Transfer conversation node; implicit triggers when intent is not matched or the user asks for an agent; full conversation history and context variables passed to the live agent.

title: Messenger Platform policy overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 24-hour standard messaging window; Human Agent tag for manual replies within 7 days; automated chats must disclose where the law requires (start, after a lapse, when switching from human to automated) and it is recommended best practice; bots respond within 30 seconds; window and some tags apply to the Instagram Messaging API.

title: WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy (last updated 23 September 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Automation allowed in the 24-hour window with prompt, clear and direct escalation paths (in-chat transfer, phone, email, web, store, form); opt-in required; honour opt-outs; only approved templates outside the window.

title: Knowledge in GPTs (search result title: Creating and editing GPTs)
supports: Search-confirmed (fetch blocked with HTTP 403): a search result showed this exact page. A GPT can hold up to 20 knowledge files of up to 512 MB each.

title: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) for Projects
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Projects switch to RAG automatically as knowledge nears the context limit; up to 10 times more content; paid plans only; tips on file names and grouping.

title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval (19 September 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Chunks lose context; contextual embeddings cut failed top-20 retrievals by 35%, plus contextual BM25 by 49%, plus reranking by 67%; under about 200,000 tokens, include the whole knowledge base in the prompt.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (NeurIPS 2020)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. RAG combines a language model with a retrieved document index and produces more specific and factual text than the model alone.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (2023)
publisher: Nelson F. Liu et al., arXiv (published in TACL)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Performance is highest when relevant information is at the start or end of the context and drops when it is in the middle.

title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
supports: Opened with WebFetch. LLM01 Prompt Injection through LLM10 Unbounded Consumption, including sensitive information disclosure, excessive agency, system prompt leakage and misinformation.

title: NIST AI 600-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (July 2024)
publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch and read with a text extractor. Lists 12 generative AI risks; defines confabulation as confidently stated but erroneous or false content.

title: The User Experience of Chatbots (25 November 2018)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Qualitative study with 8 US participants; bots fail off script, lose context and hide that they are bots; recommendations to disclose, state capabilities, tolerate typos, offer buttons and free text, and offer an escape hatch to a person.

title: Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction (CHI 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Authors, CHI 2019 honourable mention; 18 design guidelines validated with 49 design practitioners against 20 AI-infused products.

title: Paul Grice (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, revised 19 June 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The cooperative principle and the maxims of quantity, quality, relation and manner; Logic and Conversation (1975) and Studies in the Way of Words (1989).
